stimulus.text: I was soon put down under the decks, and there I received such a salutation in my nostrils as I had never experienced in my life: so that, with the loathsomeness of the stench, and crying together, I became so sick and low that I was not able to eat, nor had I the least desire to taste any thing. I now wished for the last friend, death, to relieve me…

books.section: British Empire in America: Growth and Conflict (1650-1750)

primary_sources: Olaudah Equiano, The Interesting Narrative of the Life of Olaudah Equiano (1789)

stem: Equiano's account describes enslaved people packed below deck in filth, so sick they could not eat. A diagram of the Brookes, drawn in 1788, shows rows of people packed shoulder to shoulder, with 2 feet 7 inches between the beams. What does the agreement between these two sources best show?

options.text: Both sources were written by the same author in the same year
options.misconception: Confuses two sources with one author; Equiano and the diagram's makers were different people.

options.text: The Brookes diagram copied Equiano's words and turned them into a drawing
options.misconception: Confuses agreement with copying; the diagram measures, it does not quote Equiano.

options.text: Two independent sources agree on the overcrowding of the Middle Passage
The Middle Passage was comfortable for most of the captives who crossed
options.misconception: Reverses what the sources show; both describe packing and sickness, not comfort.

rationales.general:
1. Name the two sources. Equiano's memoir is a firsthand account; the Brookes diagram is a measured plan.
2. Check their independence. Different authors, different kinds of evidence, made in different years.
3. Find the agreement. Both show people packed tight below deck — one in words, one in measurements.
4. Draw the lesson. When independent sources agree, the shared claim grows stronger.
Remember: corroboration is two independent sources saying the same thing — not one source said twice.
rationales.A: Equiano wrote a memoir; the diagram was drawn by abolitionists. Different authors made the two sources.
rationales.B: A diagram measures and draws; it does not copy words. The agreement is in the facts, not the phrasing.
rationales.C: A firsthand account and a measured diagram, made independently, both show the same overcrowding.
rationales.D: Both sources show packing and sickness, not comfort. Agreement on cruelty is not evidence of comfort.
